key_idea: An infinite self-avoiding walk with bounded steps cannot avoid all prime multiples because doing so would require the walk's trajectory to generate more entropy than its bounded steps can supply.
reason: The proof brilliantly recasts a notoriously difficult number-theoretic geometry problem into the language of information theory, achieving a profound cross-field unification. Although making the entropy budget rigorous requires a somewhat intricate chain of technical lemmas and careful bookkeeping over sampling batches, the overarching argument relies on deeply elegant and conceptual ideas rather than brute force.
